title: OKR stress-test scenarios and townline rehearsal notes v0.1
content:
Purpose:
- Create a small set (3) of concise stress-test scenarios to validate OKR messaging and escalation flows ahead of the Q3 townline.
- Capture a lean rehearsal run-of-show, ownership, and fallback language for execs and comms to use if scenarios materialize.

Background/context:
- We declare a small set of high-impact OKRs for Q3 across Hosted API growth, Dedicated bookings, and Private deployment pilots.
- Senior execs want to be confident we can answer: what happens if demand outstrips capacity; what if a regression in latency/quality is detected; what if a major customer needs an emergency private deployment?
- This doc is intentionally tactical — short scripts for spokes, triggers (metrics), owners, + fallback messages.

Audience:
- Execs presenting the townline (CTO, Head of Product, CRO), comms, SRE on-call leads, product owners for Hosted/Dedicated/Private.

SCENARIOS (short + comm scripts + owners)

Scenario 1 — High-demand spike (bursting beyond Dedicated capacity):
- Trigger: sustained 30% above peak token throughput for 6 hours OR 25% increase in 1h with rising queueing latency (P95 > 250ms for request phase). Metric refs: token/s, queue depth, P95 latency.
- Immediate impact: Increased latency for some Hosted customers; Dedicated pools approaching autoscale ceiling.
- Owner: Marcus Rivera (Infra) + Head of Dedicated Sales (Priya Nair) for customer comms.
- Mitigation actions (first 60m): prioritize critical tenants (tiering), enable short-burst capacity (pre-approved burst credit), route non-time-critical batch jobs to lower-cost pools.
- Exec-facing script (2 lines): "We’re seeing an unprecedented demand burst that’s stressing capacity. We’ve activated prioritized routing and short-burst capacity; most teams will see improved latency in the next 30–60 minutes. We’ll update at the 1-hour mark."
- Fallback message (if >3h): "We’re still under active load; we’ve temporarily limited lower-priority batch jobs and are offering partners a migration window to Dedicated pools. If latency persists we’ll open a ticket for individual customers."
- Escalation: If >4h, convene incident briefing with SRE + sales + product and prepare a formal customer advisory. Link to incident channel: RED-4821.

Scenario 2 — Quality regression detected in a verified model variant (embedding drift / generation hallucination upward of threshold):
- Trigger: Automated evals show a 12% regression on the core prompt set AND at least two customer-reported quality complaints in 24h.
- Immediate impact: Some product flows (autocomplete, summarization) degrade; potential downstream SLA breaches for precision-sensitive customers.
- Owner: Aisha Patel (Applied ML) + Product-hosted-api (Liam Chen).
- Mitigation actions: disable problematic model variant rollout, rollback to previous pinned version, activate quality monitoring alert to affected routes, notify customers on monitored list.
- Exec-facing script: "A model variant deployed for latency gains is underperforming on our core eval set for a subset of prompts. We’ve rolled traffic back to the verified baseline while we investigate—customers on higher tiers are being notified directly."
- Fallback message (if rollback incomplete after 2h): "We’re expanding the rollback and applying temporary token-level throttles for affected routes. Expect updates every 90 minutes."
- Escalation: If customer-impacting errors continue past 6h, schedule a customer-facing incident report and prepare remediation credits/comp package. Link to ticket RED-4902.

Scenario 3 — Private deployment onboarding delay for a regulated customer (compliance / networking block):
- Trigger: Private deployment network validation fails for two consecutive handoffs; deployment >5 business days behind committed start date.
- Immediate impact: SLA/contract risk; sales and customer success escalations.
- Owner: Priya Nair (Sales Ops) + Marcus Rivera (Infra Private).
- Mitigation actions: raise to private-deployments fast-track (pre-approved credits for field eng), assign a designated on-site liaison, and offer temporary hosted-sandbox with strict data handling safeguards.
- Exec-facing script: "We’ve encountered network validation blockers for a large private deployment. We’ve assembled a cross-functional field team and offered a temporary hosted sandbox to keep the customer moving forward while we resolve networking."
- Fallback message (if unresolved after 3 business days): "We’ll propose a compensatory cadence and extended support package; legal and sales are coordinating contract remedies."

Townline (all-company) run-of-show for rehearsals and associated notes:
- Length: 50 minutes (exec updates 25m, Q&A 20m, quickbreak 5m).
- Speakers + order: CEO/CTO open (5m) -> Product lead (Hosted/Dedicated/Private) (10m) -> Infra & SRE (5m) -> GTM snapshot (Remainder) -> Q&A.
- Rehearsal cadence: two dry-runs with execs + one full dress with tech staging and comms 48h before townline.
- Rehearsal schedule (owners):
  - Dry-run #1 (execs only): July 8, 10:00–11:00 — Owner: Sofie Lind
  - Dry-run #2 (with SRE & product leads): July 10, 14:00–15:30 — Owner: Marcus Rivera
  - Full dress (with comms + stage ops): July 14, 09:00–10:30 — Owner: Aisha Patel
- Slide note highlights and cadence tips for speakers:
  - Keep scenario language one-liners; avoid jargon (ex: use "latency increases" not P95 unless question prompts it).
  - If asked about remediation timeline, default to committed SLAs + transparent ETA ranges (e.g., 30–90m, 2–6h, multi-day).
  - Call out customer support path explicitly (support.redwood.ai, and the priority contact alias).
- Q&A prep: seed three likely tough questions and suggested answers:
  1) Will customers be compensated if we miss SLAs? -> Standard approach: case-by-case; mention remediation credit framework.
  2) How are we preventing future model quality regressions? -> Point to invest in automated evals + canary rollouts + rollback policies.
  3) When will Dedicated capacity be expanded? -> Call out committed capacity roadmap and near-term burst knobs.

Staging & comms checklist (before show):
- Tech: verify prod/staging video routing, test stream latency using local device from three regions.
- Comms: publish a 1-paragraph pre-read to staff (what to expect, who to ping) 24h before. Owner: Liam Chen.
- Kickoff: confirm execs accept scripted fallback lines. Owner: Sofie Lind.
- Incident readiness: ensure SRE on-call is reachable and incident channel pinned. Owner: Marcus Rivera.

Open questions / unresolved decisions:
- Do we want a formalized, single-template customer advisory for each scenario? (pros: speed + consistency; cons: legal review lag). Owner: Comms + Legal (Priya to coordinate).
- Thresholds: confirm exact numbers for P95 latency and token/s that map to the scenario triggers (currently draft metrics above). Owner: Infra (Marcus) + Product (Liam).
- Compensation policy trigger thresholds for model regressions — product + finance to sign off. Owner: Finance (TBD).

Next steps (this week):
- Finalize scenario thresholds and short scripts (Marcus/Liam by July 2).
- Run dry-run #1 (Sofie to schedule invites by June 16).
- Draft pre-read + FAQ to staff and execs (Liam/Aisha by June 25).
- Create incident channel templates and pre-fill linked ticket keys (Marcus by June 20).

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep language plain — townline audience is broad.
- Don’t bury the certainty: say what we know, and what we’re doing.
- Rehearse timing tightly; 2m per slide estimate.

Attachments / quick refs:
- Eval suite summary: see Confluence link above.
- Incident tickets examples: RED-4821, RED-4902.
